column1: # Setting patches (dm/games/README.md, Setting patches): words of the game's code the host writes at launch when a setting has a value, each after checking the original word on the build it was found in.
# Render resolution (README.md, Upscaler and resolution). The scene is the output (2560x1440 docked, 1920x1080 handheld) times a scale the dynamic-resolution controller picks each
# frame from its level palette (RomFS ModelSceneExtensionParam: 0.75 down to 0.333 docked, to 0.4445 handheld; never 1.0), built at stage start from the palette's level entries
# (main+0x31c3b30: {scale, priority} nodes in a list at ctrl+0x190). The controller's update (main+0x805aa0) returns the scale in the low word of x0 with a level-changed flag above
# it, which its caller (main+0x31d3ee0) turns into the scene's scale (ctrl+0xe5c) whenever the level changes or the stage starts. Both of its paths return through main+0x805ff0
# (fmov w9,s8: the chosen level's scale, aligned to the controller's width step). A fixed render resolution writes the scale there (movz w9,#hi,lsl #16: the float's upper half,
# so 1.5 is 0.66797 and 1.6875 0.59375): every level then has that scale. Rate 1.0 is the game's own path without its network (NDSR's scale-1.0 branch, main+0x251440)
